messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: gtest methods
parts: What's the difference between TEST and TEST_F?  I know I can't mix them so I want to make sure I understand the difference before refactoring tests.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] gtest methods
parts:
The F in TEST_F stands for fixture. It's when you have a class that sets up reusable test code between tests.

See the Google test wiki for more details:
https://code.google.com/p/googletest/wiki/Primer#Test_Fixtures:_Using_the_Same_Data_Configuration_for_Multiple_Te

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] gtest methods
parts:
Not sure what you mean. If you want multiple tests to use the same setup code and gave shared variables, use a fixture.

If the test can stand on its own, don't use one.

One test file can have multiple fixtures. The fixtures can also be typed, which is what we use in some of our more complicated tests.
